description: For aos configuration files that use $ref/$env (for plain data use json_add). Same as json_add, but the value comes from exactly one of value / text (parsed as JSON) / from (copied from FILE#/POINTER); resolve: true resolves $ref/$env in it before storing; follow: true changes the file a $ref on the way points to; check: true refuses changes that break the aos configuration. Example: {"path": "fsm.json#/states/act/exec", "from": "lib.json#/exec"}. Details: knowledge_read aos/tools/jsonx_add.json.

path.description: FILE#/POINTER in one string, e.g. cfg.json#/states/think/next; FILE alone = the whole document; FILE#/ is the key named "" (RFC 6901). Relative files start at your workspace.

value.description: required: the new value, any JSON (string, number, boolean, null, object, array); stored exactly as given: a string stays a string

text.description: a JSON text to parse and store (instead of value), e.g. "{\"a\": true}"

from.description: FILE#/POINTER to copy the value from (instead of value)

parents.description: true = create missing objects along the way (like mkdir -p)

resolve.description: true = resolve $ref/$env inside the value before storing; false = store them as written

follow.description: true = go through $ref on the way and change the file it points to; false = a $ref/$env on the way is an error (FollowMissing)

check.description: true = refuse the change if it adds problems to the aos configuration
